summary: Reviewed the actual 64×64 portrait and all 18 poses at native 1× and the supplied nearest-neighbor 3× on light, dark and checker backgrounds. The high ponytail, navy tie, teal short jacket and long side panels, narrow red belt, blue-gray trousers and two small shoes form a consistent female swordswoman silhouette. The roughly three-head SD proportions, two eyes and eyebrows, and right-facing three-quarter face are readable. Hair highlights, sleeve folds and trouser shading give modest volume with generally upper-left illumination; the pale blade separates from the clothing, although its contrast is weaker on the light background. No obvious unintended transparent holes or broken body outlines are visible; the separation behind the ponytail and between the legs reads as intentional negative space. Standing soles share the ground line, and the collapsed pose has continuous neck/clothing and a coherent bent-leg silhouette. Windup shows an upper hilt grip, a short exposed silver blade and a lower hand at the scabbard; move and attack have a wider stride and raised versus low diagonal blades. Recover contracts the stance, while hit leans back with a changed expression. Visible hand–hilt–blade connections remain continuous. Skill preparation raises the blade across the shoulder, contact sends two thin teal branches from the actual blade tip, and recovery lowers the blade with separated residual particles. Poison bends inward with a hand over the abdomen and distressed face; stun uses slack arms, an open mouth and stars; sleep closes the eyes, lowers the head and lets the sword hang toward the ground. Their paired frames change authored posture/details rather than merely tinting the idle. Idle breathing is restrained. This is a reviewer recommendation, not the user’s selection. Static pose previews cannot establish motion timing, the drawn-idle to partly drawn-windup transition in playback, actual battle readability, or literal-grid authorship. Geometry compliance alone was not used as visual approval.
